title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 53
paragraphs: These, then, were camping around the temple of Hera. Pausanias, seeing them retiring from the camp, gave the word to the Lacedaemonians also to take up their arms and follow after the others who had gone before, supposing these were going to the agreed place. When all the other commanders were ready to obey Pausanias, Amompharetos son of Poliades, commander of the Pitanate division, said he would not flee from the strangers, nor would he willingly disgrace Sparta; he expressed wonder at what was being done, not having been present at the earlier discussion. Pausanias and Euryanax were greatly disturbed that he did not obey them — and still more that they might be forced to leave the Pitanate division behind, since he refused. They feared that, if they left it in order to carry out what they had agreed with the other Greeks, Amompharetos himself would perish being left behind, along with the men with him. With this in mind they kept the Lacedaemonian force from moving, while they tried to persuade him that it was not right for him to do this.
